messages:
amelia_cust: Hey team — our org showed 0 credits around 23:58 local time, then at 00:01 it still returned 429s even though the UI showed the monthly bucket refilled. We had a demo live, lots of streaming retries. Any clue?

jessica_cs: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the tenant id and the exact timestamps of the 429s? Also were you on websocket streaming or REST requests?

amelia_cust: tenant: org-acme-42. 429s start at 2026-03-01T23:59:12Z and continued until 00:01:05Z. We were on streaming (ws) with automatic reconnects enabled.

jessica_cs: thanks. Quick note: streaming sessions can hold tokens/reservations while reconnecting which sometimes shows as "available" in the UI after refill but requests still hit the enforcement layer. I'll ping eng.

tom_engineer: @jessica_cs looking — two likely contenders: 1) refill job ran but a cache shard didn't expire -> enforcement layer saw stale 0. 2) inflight retry storm consumed tokens as reconnects happened. Any logs / client headers we can use to correlate?

amelia_cust: attaching minimal repro snippet we used on the client: ```js
const ws = new WebSocket('wss://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?tenant=org-acme-42&key=XXX');
ws.on('close', ()=> setTimeout(()=> ws = new WebSocket(...), 200)); // naive reconnect
```

jessica_cs: helpful, thanks. For immediate mitigation: 1) disable aggressive reconnects for a minute so the enforcement layer sees the refill; 2) if you can, open a fresh websocket connection from a new client/session id — will often avoid the reservation.

sre_maya: I pulled the internal metric traces for org-acme-42. Refill job started at 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z and completed by 00:00:03Z. However, a gateway cache for auth tokens didn't update for ~45s on a single shard (metric: auth_cache_stale_shard=1). That shard was serving enforcement reads so some requests still saw 0.

amelia_cust: ugh ok — was worried it was something we did. Any ETA on fix/rollback?

sre_maya: root cause: cache invalidation missed a go-routine due to a race; we pushed a hotfix at 00:02:10Z and cleared the shard cache. We'll follow up with a postmortem. For you: we revoked the stale enforcement token and forced a refill for org-acme-42 — you should see no more 429s. Can you confirm?

amelia_cust: confirmed — traffic is flowing again, demo resumed. Thanks!! :tada:

jessica_cs: Sorry for the disruption. Follow-ups: we'll add guidance in docs about websocket reconnect backoff during reset windows and add an automatic enforcement cache flush after refill. I'll file a support ticket and CC you on the postmortem.

amelia_cust: appreciated. Also can you confirm we weren't double-billed? we saw many retries during the 0-window.

sre_maya: good question — retries while enforcement returned 429 are not billed. We confirmed consumption spikes were mostly enforcement reads and reconnect attempts that didn't decrement the monthly bucket. I'll have billing_bot verify final usage numbers.

billing_bot: FYI: created invoice-check job run for org-acme-42 (run id: r-20260301-01). No unexpected token charges observed in provisional usage. If you want a formal audit, open a ticket and we'll run a full scan.

amelia_cust: perfect — thanks everyone.
